عَلِيمٌ : see عَالِمٌ. ―
-b2- العَلِيمُ and ↓ العَالِمُ and ↓ العَلَّامُ , as epithets applied to God, signify [The Omniscient;] He who knows what has been and what will be; who ever has known, and ever will know, what has been and what will be; from whom nothing is concealed in the earth nor in the heaven; whose knowledge comprehends all things, the covert thereof and the overt, the small thereof and the great, in the most complete manner. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
